---
title: "Show data in a notebook"
guide-section: How-to guides
---

`dastor.view` shows the viewer in a Jupyter (or marimo) cell. It takes a directory, or a spool or patch you already hold, including data in memory and selections:

```python
import dascore as dc
import dastor

viewer = dastor.view(dc.get_example_spool("random_das"))  # or a patch, or "/data/das"
viewer  # the last line of a cell shows the viewer
```

## Get the annotations you drew

```python
viewer.annotations()  # the sets drawn so far, as DASCore annotation sets by "owner/name"
```

They are kept in a temporary directory until the kernel stops. Pass `annotations=` a directory to keep them.

## Open the viewer in a browser tab

`viewer.url` is the same page, for a browser tab.

## Read the same data from a script

The viewer's address carries a random token, which every request of its API must present:

```python
client = dastor.Client(viewer.address, key=viewer.token)
```

## Show another server's data

```python
dastor.view(dastor.Client("https://das.example.org", key=KEY).spool())
```

## Keep several viewers open

Each `dastor.view` closes the viewer before it, so the page keeps its address and its settings. Give each one its own `port=` to keep several open.

## Read more than the limits allow

When every patch is held in memory, a tile and a screen may read any amount. Otherwise the server's [limits](41-config.qmd#limits) apply; `limits=` sets them.

## Use a notebook on another machine

The browser can't reach the viewer's address there. Forward the port, or with jupyter-server-proxy pass `base_url="/proxy/{port}"` (not yet tried against a real proxy).

## Close it

```python
viewer.close()
```
